claims.text: A lamellar eutectic microstructure enhances the initial supply of Al during oxidation.
The lamellar structure provides directional Al reservoirs.
A lamellar eutectic structure reduces the critical Al concentration required to form a continuous Al2O3 scale.
Enhanced initial Al supply enables rapid formation of a continuous, exclusive Al2O3 scale.
Increasing Co and Cr relative to Ni toward equiatomic proportions enhances configurational entropy and lattice distortion.
High configurational entropy generates severe lattice distortion in multiprincipal-element alloys.
Severe lattice distortion associated with high configurational entropy increases vacancy formation energies.
Severe lattice distortion associated with high configurational entropy increases cation migration barriers.
The entropy-related increases in defect and migration energies suppress elemental diffusion through the Al-depletion zone during steady-state oxidation.
The entropy-related mechanism specifically suppresses sustained Al migration.
Suppressing elemental diffusion retards steady-state TGO growth.
Slower TGO growth reduces catastrophic spallation and coating-failure risk.
Conventional MCrAlY improvement strategies do not adequately address both rapid initial exclusive Al2O3 formation and prolonged suppression of TGO growth at temperatures approaching 1200°C.
Combining a eutectic microstructure with MPEA entropy effects has the potential to optimize both transient and steady-state oxidation behavior.
The proposed eutectic MPEA will form a continuous, exclusive Al2O3 scale faster than a conventional MCrAlY or standard Ni-based baseline.
The proposed eutectic MPEA will exhibit slower and more stable TGO growth than the conventional baseline.
Temperatures approaching 1200°C are a relevant regime for assessing oxidation resistance and TGO stability in next-generation turbine-engine materials.
The proposed behavior applies specifically in a high-oxygen atmosphere.
